## ENV-UAT-001 Environment Evidence

The production-like UAT environment implemented on 2026-07-27 through
2026-07-28 provides live evidence for the deployment shape used by
`DEPLOY-002`, `DEPLOY-003`, `DEPLOY-005`, `DEPLOY-009`, `DEPLOY-011`,
`AUTH-012`, `AUTH-016`, `SECRET-001` and `OPS-002` without changing their
active product requirement identities.

- Evidence: three Ready RKE2 control-plane/etcd/worker nodes; separate
  single-node Rancher management cluster; two application replicas across
  nodes; PDBs; two-replica Longhorn volumes; strict-TLS edge/OIDC/Rancher
  endpoints; full dependency readiness.
- Identity evidence: real FreeIPA LDAPS federation, restricted one-user sync,
  LDAP-origin group, audited `system-admin` mapping and one reconciled
  `external_sync` membership. First-login TOTP remains an operator checkpoint.
- Vault evidence: three unsealed Integrated Raft peers, Shamir `5/3` encrypted
  custody, Kubernetes Auth application sentinel, leader failover, revoked
  bootstrap/recovery roots and final anonymous root-generation HTTP 403.
- Recovery evidence: encrypted RKE2 etcd copies and matching hashes. A native
  Vault snapshot/isolated restore and representative datastore restores remain
  open and therefore do not close the corresponding release-acceptance rows.
- Security/release evidence: dependency and static scans pass; container
  CVE/SBOM, real provider workflows and fresh independent 80% coverage evidence
  remain open. No historical or environment evidence is used to hide those
  active gaps.

Environment acceptance can update only these execution rows and the matching
live-evidence notes on existing requirement rows. It cannot close Production,
independent HA, directory federation, backup/restore, signed-release,
container/SBOM or independent Frontend/Backend 80% coverage gates without their
own required evidence and approvals.

### ENV-LOCAL-K8S-001 Execution Evidence (2026-08-19)

- `TARGET` and `IMAGE` evidence passed, including exact cluster UID, dirty
  source fingerprint, seven arm64 images and three-node local-image execution.
- `PLATFORM` partially passed: ingress-nginx `4.15.1` and loopback-only Docker
  proxying are verified; five local-path PVCs are Bound, but Docker Desktop's
  VM filesystem is full and no stateful readiness claim is made.
- `PACKAGE` passed only for superseding generation `a238d55a45943084`. The
  earlier generation is retired after Base64 disclosure in command output and
  must not be reused. No application workload consumed it.
- `RELEASE` is blocked at failed foundation revision 1. Disk exhaustion and the
  OpenSearch strong-password gate prevented readiness; application stage,
  Jobs, authentication and acceptance evidence are absent.
- Continuation is separately gated on approval for non-destructive Docker disk
  expansion/restart and a strong random OpenSearch-only Secret override. No
  cleanup or global release-gate claim is implied.
- After that pause, Peter separately authorized deletion of all Minikube data.
  `minikube delete --all --purge` removed both known profiles and
  `/Users/peter/.minikube`; verification found only the `docker-desktop`
  kubeconfig context and no Minikube-labeled Docker resources or
  Minikube/`kicbase` image. This later host cleanup does not change the earlier
  installation non-interference result and did not mutate the NomoSmart Helm
  release, its five Bound PVCs or unrelated Docker resources.
- Peter then separately requested complete Minikube uninstallation. Homebrew
  `minikube 1.38.1` was removed with `brew uninstall minikube` (11 files,
  135.7 MB); final verification found no executable, installed formula or
  Minikube data directory while `docker-desktop` and all five PVCs remained.
